column1: # One row per file in upstream lily/ (LilyPond 2.27.2, the pinned reference), so the
# remaining engine work is COMPUTED rather than remembered. EPG0 built it; every later
# EPG session updates the rows it lands.
#   3 detail        ported  -> the C# file(s) carrying it, ';'-separated, repo-relative
#                   group   -> the EPG group that owes it
#                   no-port -> why it has no analogue in the port
#   4 notes         free text; blank for the ordinary cases
# Fences (LedgerTests): every upstream file has exactly one row, every 'ported' target
# exists on disk, every 'group' names a real EPG group, and the row set equals the
# A 'ported' row means the file's TYPE and ALGORITHMS are carried. It does NOT assert
# that the file's LY_DEFINE surface is complete -- the bindings rule (standing rule 3)
# owes that in the same session, and entry-point closure is measured separately against
# Totals: 448 files = 137 ported + 282 grouped + 29 no-port. (EPG0 opened at 88/331/29;
# EPG1 left 90/329/29; EPG2 and EPG3's first slice moved twenty rows on 2026-08-05;
# EPG3's finish moved five more the same day: paper-outputter(+scheme),
# function-documentation, lily-version, general-scheme. EPG4 moved twelve. EPG13 moved
# stencil-integral, and the four font *-scheme files.)
# Read this file through PortLedger rather than counting by eye -- these totals are a
# convenience, and LedgerTests computes the real ones.
